deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page is the end of Riemann's letter to Weierstrass, dated Göttingen 26 October 1859: 'Beweis des Satzes, dass eine einwerthige mehr als 2n-fach periodische Function von n Veränderlichen unmöglich ist'. It was published posthumously in Crelle 71 (1870) and in the Gesammelte Werke.

Setting. A 'Modulsystem' a_mu = (a_mu^1, ..., a_mu^n) in C^n is a simultaneous period of a single-valued analytic function f of n complex variables. Equivalently it is a vector in R^{2n}. 'Congruent nach den Modulsystemen' means differing by an integer combination of periods. 'Inhalt des periodisch wiederkehrenden Gebiets' is the 2n-dimensional volume of a fundamental parallelotope, i.e. |det| of the 2n real period vectors.

What the previous page established. Assume there are 2n+1 periods.
- If they satisfy no integer relation, a pigeonhole (Dirichlet) argument applies: divide [0,1)^{2n} into q^{2n} cells. Then f is invariant under arbitrarily small translations, so it depends on fewer than n linear forms.
- So assume integer relations Sum_{mu=1}^{2n+1} a_mu^nu m_mu = 0 (nu = 1..n).
- Lemma begun there: if m_1..m_{2n} are coprime, the vector b_1 = Sum_{mu<=2n} m_mu a_mu can be completed to a basis b_1..b_{2n} of the same lattice. Proof by successive gcd steps: with beta m_1 - alpha m_2 = theta_1, set c_1 = (m_1 a_1 + m_2 a_2)/theta_1 and b_{2n} = alpha a_1 + beta a_2. Then a_1 = beta c_1 - (m_2/theta_1) b_{2n} and a_2 = -alpha c_1 + (m_1/theta_1) b_{2n}. This is a unimodular change; iterate with theta_2 = gcd(theta_1, m_3), and so on.

This page.
(1) This completes the lemma ('der zu beweisende Satz'). The new basis b generates the same lattice. The fundamental volume is unchanged, since the transition matrix is integral with determinant ±1.

(2) Reduction of the relation [my filling]. Let theta = gcd(m_1..m_{2n}) and b_1 = (1/theta) Sum_{mu<=2n} m_mu a_mu, completed to a basis b_1..b_{2n}. The relation becomes theta b_1 + m_{2n+1} a_{2n+1} = 0. Divide by gcd(theta, m_{2n+1}) and fix signs. This gives Riemann's form p b_1 - q a_{2n+1} = 0 with gcd(p,q) = 1.

(3) Merging two periods. Choose integers gamma, delta with p delta + q gamma = 1. Put c = gamma b_1 + delta a_{2n+1}. Using a_{2n+1} = (p/q) b_1:
- c = b_1 (gamma q + delta p)/q = b_1/q = a_{2n+1}/p.
- Conversely b_1 = q c and a_{2n+1} = p c.
So Z b_1 + Z a_{2n+1} = Z c. All integer combinations of a_1..a_{2n+1} are exactly the integer combinations of the 2n vectors c = b_1/q, b_2, ..., b_{2n}. Replacing b_1 by b_1/q divides the determinant by |q|. So the fundamental volume becomes 1/q of that of a_1..a_{2n}.

(4) Iteration. Each further period linked to the current 2n by integer relations again yields 2n generators. The volume is divided each time by an integer (an 'aliquot part').
- If the volume tends to 0, the period group is not discrete. Then f (continuous) is invariant under arbitrarily small translations, hence under a real subspace. f then depends on fewer than n linear forms ('n-1, n-2, ..., n-m' according as 1, 2, ..., m dimensions become infinitely small).
- Excluding such degenerate functions, the process must stop. One then obtains 2n periods generating all periods of f.

Conclusion of the letter: a non-degenerate single-valued function of n variables has at most 2n independent periods.
errors: No algebraic error: gamma b_1 + delta a_{2n+1} = a_{2n+1}/p = b_1/q follows correctly from p b_1 = q a_{2n+1} and p delta + q gamma = 1.
Missing superscript slip: 'delta a_{2n+1}' should be 'delta a_{2n+1}^nu'.

Implicit step: the passage from the n relations Sum a_mu^nu m_mu = 0 to the form p b_1 - q a_{2n+1} = 0 needs b_1 := (1/gcd(m_1..m_{2n})) Sum m_mu a_mu (so the lemma's coprimality hypothesis holds) and division by gcd(theta, m_{2n+1}). Riemann leaves this unstated.
The case q = ±1 (a_{2n+1} already in the lattice) gives no reduction. That is harmless but not mentioned.

Gap 1, termination argument: 'volume -> 0 implies some dimensions become infinitely small' needs a compactness/accumulation argument, essentially that a non-discrete subgroup of R^{2n} has closure containing a line. This is sketched, not proved.

Gap 2, termination argument: the process could also run forever with the volume staying bounded below, since the infinitely many periods are only countable. One needs the observation that the volume, a product of integer reciprocals times a fixed number, can only drop finitely many times if bounded below.

Imprecise dimension count: invariance under m real dimensions gives dependence on n minus the complex dimension of their C-span, which is not necessarily n-m. For analytic f, one real line of invariance already gives a complex line. The qualitative conclusion 'fewer than n linear expressions' is correct.

results.what: Unimodular basis change: a primitive integer combination of lattice generators can be completed to a basis of the same lattice, and the fundamental volume is preserved.
results.modern_name: Completion of a primitive vector to a basis of Z^k / unimodular (GL_k(Z)) basis change
results.usually_credited_to: Classical (Gauss, Hermite, Smith; standard in lattice theory)

results.what: Merging two commensurable periods p b = q a into one generator b/q via Bezout; the covolume is divided by q.
results.modern_name: Bezout reduction / finitely generated subgroup of a lattice is a lattice; index computation
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi (1835) for n=1; Riemann's 1859 letter for n variables

results.what: A single-valued analytic function of n variables with more than 2n independent periods is degenerate (depends on fewer than n linear forms).
results.modern_name: Discreteness of the period group: Jacobi–Riemann–Weierstrass theorem on 2n-fold periodicity
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi (n=1, 1835); Riemann (letter to Weierstrass, 26 Oct 1859, publ. Crelle 71, 1870); Weierstrass

deep.surprise_reason: This is the final page of Riemann's well-known letter to Weierstrass of 26 October 1859. It was published in Crelle's Journal 71 (1870) and in his Gesammelte Werke, and the result is standardly attributed to him (with Jacobi for n=1).

checkable.sympy: p,q,g,d,b=symbols('p q gamma delta b'); simplify((g*b + d*(p*b/q)).subs(g,(1-p*d)/q) - b/q)
checkable.asserts: gamma*b_1 + delta*a_{2n+1} = b_1/q when a_{2n+1} = p*b_1/q and p*delta + q*gamma = 1.

checkable.sympy: p,q,d,b=symbols('p q delta b'); simplify(((1-p*d)/q*b + d*(p*b/q)) - (p*b/q)/p)
checkable.asserts: The merged generator also equals a_{2n+1}/p.

checkable.sympy: m1,m2,al,be=symbols('m1 m2 alpha beta'); th=be*m1-al*m2; simplify(Matrix([[m1/th, m2/th],[al, be]]).det())
checkable.asserts: The map (a1,a2) -> (c1=(m1 a1+m2 a2)/theta, b=alpha a1+beta a2) has determinant 1, so covolume is preserved.

checkable.sympy: m1,m2,al,be,a1,a2=symbols('m1 m2 alpha beta a1 a2'); th=be*m1-al*m2; c1=(m1*a1+m2*a2)/th; B=al*a1+be*a2; simplify(be*c1 - m2/th*B - a1), simplify(-al*c1 + m1/th*B - a2)
checkable.asserts: Inverse formulas from the previous page: a1 = beta c1 - (m2/theta) b and a2 = -alpha c1 + (m1/theta) b.
Example n=1: periods 1, i, 1/3 (relation 1*1 - 3*(1/3) = 0, p=1, q=3) generate the lattice with basis 1/3, i; covolume divided by q=3.
For coprime p=5, q=7 there exist integers (delta, gamma) with 5*delta + 7*gamma = 1, as required for the merge.

transcription_corrections: 'delta a_{2n+1}' in the displayed formula: in the manuscript and by sense it should be delta a_{2n+1}^nu.
The first occurrence of '\frac{b_1^\nu}{q}' in the list of 2n Modulsysteme looks like b_1^* in the image. It should be b_1^ν (or b_1) over q.
'Der Inhalt ... ist ... dieselbe' is as written by Riemann (grammatically 'derselbe'); no correction of content needed.
'Ist die Function nun ausser diesen Modulsystemen noch ein[?]': sense requires 'Hat die Function ... noch eins'. The uncertain word is best read as 'eins' (one more Modulsystem).
'periodisch[-en-] sich wiederholenden': the deleted ending is correctly marked; read 'periodisch sich wiederholenden'.
